Here are three well-known, citable sources you can drop in a footnote (no links):

1) Boehm, B. W., Software Engineering Economics. Prentice‑Hall, 1981.  
   - Classic presentation of the “cost-to-fix” curve showing that defects become more expensive to correct the later they are found.

2) Fagan, M. E., “Design and Code Inspections to Reduce Errors in Program Development,” IBM Systems Journal, 1976.  
   - Seminal empirical study on inspections/reviews demonstrating defect detection early in the lifecycle is efficient and reduces downstream costs.

3) Jones, C. & Bonsignour, O., The Economics of Software Quality. Addison‑Wesley, 2011.  
   - Industry data and analysis on defect-removal economics and the ROI of finding defects earlier.

If you’d like these formatted in a particular citation style (APA, Chicago, IEEE), tell me which one and I’ll format them.
